requirements.desc: SHA-256 digest correctness for single-block message (NIST KAT 'abc' = ba7816bf...f20015ad)
SHA-256 empty-message digest (e3b0c442...7852b855)
SHA-256 multi-block 'abcdbcde...nopq' digest (248d6a61...19db06c1)
SHA-256 1,000,000-byte 'a' message (15626 blocks) digest (cdc76e5c...c7112cd0) via INIT+NEXT
SHA-224 truncated digest with distinct NIST init constants (CTRL.MODE=0); 'abc' = 23097d22...e36c9da7 (224-bit)
SHA-224 multi-block message + 1M-byte 'a' (224-bit) via INIT+NEXT
SHA-224 DIGEST7 (0x27) reads back 0 (truncation handled on read side)
512-bit message block loaded via BLOCK0..15 (0x10-0x1F), BLOCK0 = most-significant word (big-endian)
Multi-block message: first block INIT, subsequent NEXT continue from carried H[] (padding done in SW)
cs/we/address[7:0]/write_data[31:0] -> read_data[31:0]/error register-file access
CTRL register: bit0=INIT, bit1=NEXT, bit2=MODE; reads back {mode,next,init}; INIT priority over NEXT
STATUS register: bit0=READY (idle), bit1=VALID (completed digest)
SW writes BLOCK, writes CTRL INIT/NEXT, polls STATUS.READY then reads DIGEST; handshake liveness verified across 1021 vectors
Synchronous active-LOW reset -> FSM idle, registers default, STATUS.READY=1 after release
Read of undefined address (e.g. 0x7f) asserts error=1; defined read keeps error=0
66 cycles per 512-bit block (1 load + 64 rounds + 1 finalize); READY deasserts during compute, reasserts on completion
Big-endian word packing: BLOCK0=W[0]=MSW; DIGEST0=H0=top 32 bits
Message-length boundaries 1/55/56/64/119/120/1024 bytes (both SHA-256 and SHA-224)
>=1000 random messages (len 0-2KB) vs Python hashlib golden, 100% binary match
INIT issued during BUSY is ignored (core launches only from idle); original result intact
